references.text: The Israelites' complaints against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness, where God hears their grumbling - the same theme as הֵמָּה מַלִּינִים (they grumble)
The people quarrel with Moses and complain about lack of water, another example of Israel's repeated grumbling in the wilderness
The immediate context where the children of Israel grumbled (וַיִּלֹּנוּ) against Moses and Aaron after the report from the spies
The consequence of the evil congregation's grumbling - the spies who brought a bad report die by plague
Moses confronts Korah and his company about their grumbling against the Lord, using the same expression מַלִּינִים עָלָיו
The congregation of Israel grumbles again against Moses and Aaron, and God responds with a plague
Moses recounts how the people grumbled in their tents and said that the Lord hated them
The psalm describes how Israel despised the pleasant land and grumbled in their tents, a poetic retelling of this event
Paul warns the Corinthians not to grumble (μηδὲ γογγύζετε) as some of the Israelites did and were killed by the destroyer
The letter to the Hebrews refers to the wilderness generation that sinned and was not allowed to enter God's rest because of unbelief
